line: Built by hand. Dialed with intention. Ridden the way it's meant to be.

aboutShort: An independent bike brand making high-performance carbon road and gravel frames, engineered in the USA for speed and adventure.
about: Gerard Cycles builds its own road and gravel bikes, including the carbon Force 100 and the Trail Force RX, each handcrafted in Kirkland. Founder John Gerard Sheehan oversees every fit himself.
The shop also does custom builds, service and upgrades, and keeps the local riding community going with workshops, group rides, race support and youth programs for riders ages 9 to 17.

aboutShort: A hot-pink, woman-owned Seattle coffee shop with locations in West Seattle and SoDo, known for playful drink names and bright, photo-ready cafes.
about: Coffee industry veteran Taylor Platt opened Lula Coffee Co. in West Seattle in 2020, with a cheerful cafe and a drive-thru, and it thrived through the pandemic. A second cafe followed in SoDo in 2023, on Airport Way South by the Old Rainier Brewery's giant R sign.

The SoDo shop is all hot-pink counters and walls, puffy clouds on the ceiling and a plush blue couch, made to feel bright on gray Seattle days. The menu covers coffee classics, teas, blended drinks and smoothies, with collagen- and vegetable-powder boosted lattes and playful drinks like Wake & Bake and Don't Huck With Me.

aboutShort: Texas-style, oak-smoked barbecue from Dallas native Jack Timmons, served across Seattle since he opened the original SoDo roadhouse.
about: Jack's BBQ is a Texas-style barbecue restaurant in Seattle, founded by Jack Timmons, a Dallas native and Texas A&M graduate who trained at the university's barbecue camp before opening his first location. The original roadhouse in SoDo, on Airport Way South, is known for oak-smoked brisket cooked low and slow in steel offset smokers over Texas post oak and Washington applewood.

The menu covers the Texas classics: brisket, spare ribs and smoked sausage on the Texas Trinity plate, plus breakfast tacos, Texas chili, corn pudding and pecan pie. Jack's has grown to several locations around the Puget Sound, including South Lake Union and Redmond, and works with local philanthropic partners throughout the year.

about: "Chrome Hearts" is named after the luxury jewelry and fashion house that has become a staple in hip-hop style. Rell Moore set the concept and a starting location, and the video was shot across Seattle in 2023, premiering on the Reel Clip YouTube channel that April.

title: Street Runner
brief: A colorful, high-energy video for "Street Runner" shot at the Washington State Fair, using the rides and neon as the set.
result: A familiar public place turned into an energetic, neon-lit music video. Released in May 2022 on Tha Baby's YouTube channel, where it has passed 16,000 views.
line: Color, movement, and energy after dark.
approach: A vibrant music video that captures the track's energy through colorful cinematography and an immersive fairground setting.
Build on the artist's location concept and planned opening, using the fair's lights, attractions and movement.
Reelclip and Miguel Manzano shot across the fairgrounds with a hyperlapse intro and performance coverage. Miguel edited; Reelclip graded.
One official music video for "Street Runner".

beats.title: The artist's fair
beats.text: Tha Baby brought the location and a planned opening. We built the camera work and the look on top, using the fair itself as the set.

beats.title: Hyperlapse, then run and gun
beats.text: A hyperlapse-style intro sets the motion, then we moved through the fairgrounds lit only by the rides and neon.

beats.title: Glow in the grade
beats.text: Miguel Manzano cut it to the track's pace, and we graded it with glow, saturation and light treatments to push the neon.

aboutShort: Tha Baby is a rapper who brought the Washington State Fair concept to "Street Runner".
about: "Street Runner" by Tha Baby, produced by UJADEN, was shot at the Washington State Fair in Puyallup and premiered on the artist's own YouTube channel in May 2022. It's streaming on Apple Music.

title: Different Time
brief: Capture SlotLifeBaby in the Tacoma-area places he knows, and make everyday spots feel cinematic through framing and color instead of effects.
result: A restrained, cinematic video where camera work and color carry the look, not post effects. Released in November 2025 on the Reel Clip YouTube channel.
line: Familiar streets. Different time. A cinematic perspective.
approach: A visually engaging video that captures the artist in familiar Tacoma-area places with a polished, cinematic look.
Build on the artist's location concept with late-night neighborhood settings, group performances and intentional framing.
We filmed across Tacoma and Spanaway, from convenience store interiors to streets and the studio, favoring tripod compositions and in-camera techniques, then built the grade.
One official music video for "Different Time".

beats.title: His own neighborhood
beats.text: SlotLifeBaby wanted to shoot where he's known: the 7-Eleven, local streets and a studio around Tacoma and Spanaway.

beats.title: Made in camera
beats.text: Mostly on a tripod, with group arrangements, unusual angles and the surroundings doing the work instead of transitions or VFX.

beats.title: One grade, many lights
beats.text: Color tied together store fluorescents, night streets and the studio into one consistent, moody look.

aboutShort: SlotLifeBaby is a Tacoma-area artist who wanted "Different Time" shot in the places he knows best.
about: "Different Time" was filmed late at night around Tacoma and Spanaway, at a neighborhood 7-Eleven, on local streets and in a studio, with friends from the community in the group scenes. It premiered on the Reel Clip YouTube channel in November 2025.
